backlog.title: Bug Fix Release — Identifier, Autostart, Handshake & Heuristic Defects
backlog.description: Fix five verified defects: Hyprland dialog identifier mismatch (Major), X11 WM_CLASS parser off-by-one (Major), unquoted Windows autostart path (Major), VID/PID change not resetting handshake (Minor), and Windows title-length heuristic using byte length instead of char count (Minor). All fixes are surgical one-liners or small-block changes grounded in confirmed codebase research (see plan/006_8f4080956ee0/bugfix/001_558dab5d68a5/architecture/).

milestones.title: Major Bug Fixes — Identifier Correctness & Autostart Safety
milestones.description: Fix the three Major-severity defects (PRD IDs 1, 2, 4) that affect rule correctness on Hyprland/X11 and autostart reliability on Windows paths containing spaces.

tasks.title: Fix Hyprland 'Show Window Information' dialog to display initial_class
tasks.description: The 'Show Window Information' dialog uses list_foreground_windows() which returns c.class, but the keyboard notification paths send initial_class. For apps where these differ (Electron, some JVM apps), users copy a value that silently fails to match. Fix: use initial_class in list_foreground_windows() for parity with the notification path.

subtasks.title: Change list_foreground_windows() to use initial_class instead of class
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_8f4080956ee0/bugfix/001_558dab5d68a5/architecture/bug_findings.md §Bug 1. The hyprland crate's Client struct (data/regular.rs L239/L241) exposes both `initial_class` (stable, set once at window creation) and `class` (mutable, can change at runtime). The notification paths in handle_window_state_change (L479) and poll_window_state (L398) use `active_window.initial_class.clone()`. The dialog path list_foreground_windows() (L559-584) uses `c.class.clone()` at L571 and `active.class.clone()` at L577.
2. INPUT: None — list_foreground_windows() is the source of dialog data. It calls Clients::get() and Client::get_active() from the hyprland crate (live IPC, cannot be mocked in unit tests without a running compositor).
3. LOGIC: In src/platforms/hyprland.rs, function list_foreground_windows(): (a) at L571 change `c.class.clone()` to `c.initial_class.clone()`; (b) at L577 change `active.class.clone()` to `active.initial_class.clone()`. Both are inside the same function. Do NOT change handle_window_state_change or poll_window_state — they already use initial_class. The existing test module at L599 has no coverage for this function (it requires live IPC); verify manually on a Hyprland session with an app where class != initial_class (e.g., some Electron apps).
4. OUTPUT: list_foreground_windows() returns Vec<(String, String)> where the first tuple element is initial_class — matching what notify_qmk sends to the keyboard firmware.
5. DOCS: none — no user-facing/config/API surface change. The fix makes the dialog MORE consistent with existing docs that already say 'window class'.

tasks.title: Fix X11 WM_CLASS parser off-by-one (returns instance instead of class)
tasks.description: The WM_CLASS parser in x11.rs filters xprop output with split('"').filter(|s| !s.is_empty()), but the leading space and the ', ' separator are non-empty, shifting indices so .get(1) returns the instance string instead of the class string.

subtasks.title: Fix parser to return class and add unit tests
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_8f4080956ee0/bugfix/001_558dab5d68a5/architecture/bug_findings.md §Bug 2. In src/platforms/x11.rs L68-74, the parser does: `let quoted: Vec<&str> = rest.split('"').filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).collect();` then `quoted.get(1)`. For xprop output `WM_CLASS(STRING) = "instance", "Class"`, after split_once('=') rest = ` "instance", "Class"`. split('"') yields `[" ", "instance", ", ", "Class", ""]`; after filter(non-empty) = `[" ", "instance", ", ", "Class"]`; .get(1) = "instance" (WRONG — should be "Class").
2. INPUT: The `rest` string from `line.split_once('=').map(|(_, r)| r)` for a line starting with `WM_CLASS`. Format: ` "instance", "Class"` (leading space, comma-separated quoted strings). The `_NET_WM_NAME` parsing branch (L78-82) is UNRELATED and must NOT change.
3. LOGIC: Replace the split-on-quote approach with split-on-comma: extract a pure helper `fn parse_wm_class(rest: &str) -> Option<String>` that does `rest.split(',').map(|s| s.trim().trim_matches('"')).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).collect::<Vec<_>>().get(1).or_else(|| parts.first())`. For rest = ` "instance", "Class"`: split(',') → `[' "instance"', ' "Class"']` → trim + trim_matches('"') → `['instance', 'Class']` → .get(1) = 'Class' ✓. Call this helper from the `if line.starts_with("WM_CLASS")` branch. Add a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block (x11.rs currently has NONE) with tests: (a) typical `"firefox", "Firefox"` → returns "Firefox"; (b) single-field degenerate case → falls back to first; (c) empty/whitespace rest → None or empty.
4. OUTPUT: The app_class fed to WindowInfo::new(app_class, title) is the **class** (e.g., "Firefox") not the instance (e.g., "firefox").
5. DOCS: none — the fix makes behavior match docs that already say 'window class' (docs/configuration.md L281, docs/troubleshooting.md L571).

tasks.title: Quote Windows autostart path in both autostart.rs and the Inno installer
tasks.description: Both src/autostart.rs enable() and the Inno installer [Registry] section write the HKCU Run key value as an unquoted path. If the install path contains spaces (e.g., C:\Users\John Doe\...), the Run key may fail to execute on login or become a security vector (unquoted path traversal).

subtasks.title: Quote the exe path in src/autostart.rs current_exe_wide()
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_8f4080956ee0/bugfix/001_558dab5d68a5/architecture/bug_findings.md §Bug 3A. src/autostart.rs is entirely #[cfg(target_os = "windows")]. current_exe_wide() (L57) calls std::env::current_exe(), then encodes the OsStr as UTF-16 with a trailing NUL. enable() (L72) writes this buffer directly as REG_SZ data via RegSetValueExW (L103). is_enabled() (L38) checks value PRESENCE via RegGetValueW, not content — so quoting does NOT break the presence check.
2. INPUT: The resolved exe path from std::env::current_exe().
3. LOGIC: Modify current_exe_wide() (or the enable() call site) so the UTF-16 buffer encodes `"<path>"` — i.e., chain a leading `"` (0x0022) before the path's encode_wide() iterator, then the path chars, then a trailing `"` (0x0022), then the NUL (0x0000). The resulting REG_SZ data is e.g. `"C:\Users\John Doe\AppData\Local\Programs\QMKonnect\QMKonnect.exe"`. Test: assert current_exe_wide() starts with 0x0022 and the char before the final NUL is 0x0022.
4. OUTPUT: The HKCU Run key value is a quoted path. is_enabled() continues to work (presence-based). disable() is unaffected (it deletes the value).
5. DOCS: none — internal quoting fix. docs/troubleshooting.md L265 shows a `reg query` command to check the entry, not the value format.

subtasks.title: Quote the path in packaging/windows/inno/QMKonnect.iss [Registry] section
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_8f4080956ee0/bugfix/001_558dab5d68a5/architecture/bug_findings.md §Bug 3B. The [Registry] section of packaging/windows/inno/QMKonnect.iss currently writes: `ValueData: "{app}\{#MyAppExeName}"` (unquoted). {app} expands to the install dir (DefaultDirName = {localappdata}\Programs\QMKonnect), which can contain spaces if the username does.
2. INPUT: Inno Setup constants {app} and {#MyAppExeName} ("QMKonnect.exe").
3. LOGIC: In the [Registry] section line for the Run key, change ValueData to use Inno's `""` escape for literal double-quotes: `ValueData: """{app}\{#MyAppExeName}"""`. Inno resolves `""` to a single `"` in the final registry value, producing `"C:\...\QMKonnect.exe"`. Keep ValueType: string, ValueName: "QMKonnect", and Flags: uninsdeletevalue unchanged. This MUST match P1.M1.T3.S1's quoting so the installer and the in-app toggle write the same format.
4. OUTPUT: Fresh installs and upgrades via QMKonnect-Setup.exe write a quoted path to the HKCU Run key.
5. DOCS: none — no user-facing surface change. The installer comment already documents the Run key contract.

milestones.title: Minor Bug Fixes — Handshake Reset & Title Heuristic
milestones.description: Fix the two Minor-severity defects (PRD IDs 3, 5): VID/PID change in Settings not resetting handshake state (multi-board case), and Windows should_ignore_window title-length heuristic counting bytes instead of characters.

tasks.title: Reset handshake state when VID/PID changes in Settings (all platforms)
tasks.description: When multiple capable boards are present and the user switches VID/PID in Settings, no plug/unplug event fires, so the PresenceTracker Gain/Loss loop never re-handshakes. The stale CALLBACK_NAMES map from the old board persists for the new board. Fix: call reset_handshake_state() + perform_handshake() in each platform's save path when VID/PID actually changes.

subtasks.title: Add reset_handshake_state() + perform_handshake() to Windows tray save path (tray.rs)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_8f4080956ee0/bugfix/001_558dab5d68a5/architecture/bug_findings.md §Bug 4. The Windows save path in src/tray.rs (~L970-989) merges VID/PID onto `current_config` via `let mut merged = current_config;` (MOVES current_config), then writes via `crate::core::atomic_write(config_path, &config_content)?;`. reset_handshake_state() is pub at notifier.rs:814 (clears HOST_CAPABLE, BOARD_HAS_RULES, CALLBACK_NAMES, HAS_HANDSHAKED). perform_handshake(verbose) is pub at notifier.rs:353.
2. INPUT: The pre-save VID/PID (from current_config BEFORE the move into merged) and the post-save VID/PID (merged.vendor_id / merged.product_id). The `verbose` variable is in scope in the tray save function.
3. LOGIC: BEFORE `let mut merged = current_config;`, snapshot `let old_vid = current_config.vendor_id; let old_pid = current_config.product_id;`. AFTER `crate::core::atomic_write(config_path, &config_content)?;` succeeds, add: `if merged.vendor_id != old_vid || merged.product_id != old_pid { crate::core::notifier::reset_handshake_state(); crate::core::notifier::perform_handshake(verbose); }`. The `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]` gate on this function means the import is already available.
4. OUTPUT: The global CALLBACK_NAMES map is cleared and rebuilt for the newly-selected board immediately after a VID/PID change, without waiting for a replug event.
5. DOCS: none — internal handshake lifecycle change.

subtasks.title: Add reset_handshake_state() + perform_handshake() to macOS tray save path (tray.rs)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_8f4080956ee0/bugfix/001_558dab5d68a5/architecture/bug_findings.md §Bug 4. The macOS save path in src/tray.rs (~L1870-1885) uses the same pattern as Windows: `let mut merged = current_config;` (MOVES current_config), then merges chosen/manual VID/PID, then writes via `crate::core::atomic_write(config_path, &config_content)?;`. This function is `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]`.
2. INPUT: The pre-save VID/PID (from current_config BEFORE the move) and the post-save merged.vendor_id / merged.product_id.
3. LOGIC: BEFORE `let mut merged = current_config;`, snapshot old VID/PID. AFTER `crate::core::atomic_write(config_path, &config_content)?;` succeeds, add the same guard: `if merged.vendor_id != old_vid || merged.product_id != old_pid { crate::core::notifier::reset_handshake_state(); crate::core::notifier::perform_handshake(verbose); }`. Use whatever `verbose` variable is in scope (check the function signature / surrounding code — it may be a closure variable or module-level).
4. OUTPUT: Same as P1.M2.T1.S1 — stale name map cleared and rebuilt for the new board on macOS.
5. DOCS: none — internal handshake lifecycle change.

subtasks.title: Add reset_handshake_state() + perform_handshake() to Linux tray save path (linux_tray.rs)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_8f4080956ee0/bugfix/001_558dab5d68a5/architecture/bug_findings.md §Bug 4. The Linux save path is `fn save_and_notify(vendor_id: Option<u16>, product_id: Option<u16>)` at src/linux_tray.rs L718. It calls write_config(vendor_id, product_id) (L725) then apply_device_rule. `verbose` is NOT in scope here (save_and_notify takes only vid/pid). The existing helper `fn current_vidpid() -> Option<(u16, u16)>` at L988-1012 reads the current config's VID/PID.
2. INPUT: The new vendor_id/product_id passed to save_and_notify, and the pre-save VID/PID from current_vidpid() called BEFORE write_config.
3. LOGIC: At the top of the `Ok(path) => { ... }` arm (after write_config succeeds, L726), add: read old VID/PID via `let old = current_vidpid();` (NOTE: call this BEFORE write_config or its result is already stale — actually write_config already wrote, so snapshot BEFORE write_config at the top of save_and_notify). Compare old vs new. If changed: `crate::core::notifier::reset_handshake_state(); crate::core::notifier::perform_handshake(false);` (pass false for verbose since it's not in scope; alternatively add a `verbose: bool` param to save_and_notify and update its two call sites at L856 and L925).
4. OUTPUT: Same as P1.M2.T1.S1/S2 — stale name map cleared and rebuilt for the new board on Linux.
5. DOCS: none — internal handshake lifecycle change.

tasks.title: Fix Windows should_ignore_window title-length heuristic to count characters
tasks.description: should_ignore_window() in windows.rs uses window_info.title.len() which counts bytes, not characters. A 1-char emoji title (4 bytes) is kept while a 1-char ASCII title (1 byte) is dropped — inconsistent behavior.

subtasks.title: Change .len() to .chars().count() and add unit tests for should_ignore_window
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_8f4080956ee0/bugfix/001_558dab5d68a5/architecture/bug_findings.md §Bug 5. should_ignore_window() in src/platforms/windows.rs checks `if window_info.title.len() < 2 && !window_info.title.is_empty() { return true; }`. Rust String::len() returns BYTE length. WindowInfo is defined in src/core/types.rs (fields: app_class: String, title: String). The file is entirely #[cfg(target_os = "windows")] — tests will only compile/run on Windows.
2. INPUT: A &WindowInfo reference with .app_class and .title fields.
3. LOGIC: Change `window_info.title.len() < 2` to `window_info.title.chars().count() < 2`. Add a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block (windows.rs currently has NONE) with tests for should_ignore_window: (a) empty title with non-allowed class → true (ignored); (b) empty title with allowed class (e.g., "Chrome_WidgetWin_1") → false (kept); (c) 1-char ASCII title (e.g., "x") → true (ignored, 1 char < 2); (d) 1-char emoji title (e.g., "😀", 4 bytes) → true (ignored, 1 char < 2 — this is the FIX: previously it was 4 bytes ≥ 2 so it was KEPT); (e) 2-char title (e.g., "ab") → false (kept); (f) internal class name (e.g., "Shell_TrayWnd") with any title → true. Construct WindowInfo via WindowInfo::new(class, title).
4. OUTPUT: should_ignore_window() consistently ignores titles shorter than 2 CHARACTERS regardless of UTF-8 byte length.
5. DOCS: none — internal heuristic fix.
